title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
authors: Alexey Dosovitskiy, Lucas Beyer, Alexander Kolesnikov, Dirk Weissenborn, Xiaohua Zhai, Thomas Unterthiner, Mostafa Dehghani, Matthias Minderer, Georg Heigold, Sylvain Gelly, Jakob Uszkoreit, Neil Houlsby
conclusions: Introduces the Vision Transformer (ViT): a pure Transformer applied directly to sequences of fixed-size image patches (linear patch embedding + learnable position embeddings + class token), with no convolutional inductive bias beyond patch extraction.
Defines the ViT-Base/Large/Huge model family and the patch-size naming convention (e.g. ViT-B/16 = Base variant, 16x16 patches) used throughout the paper (Table 1).
Shows ViT underperforms comparable ResNets when trained from scratch on mid-sized data (e.g. ImageNet only) due to lack of translation-equivariance/locality inductive bias.

Shows that with large-scale pre-training (ImageNet-21k or JFT-300M), ViT matches or beats state-of-the-art CNN baselines (BiT-ResNet, Noisy Student) on ImageNet, CIFAR-10/100, Oxford Pets/Flowers, and the 19-task VTAB suite, while using substantially less pre-training compute.
Provides a compute-vs-performance scaling study showing Transformers dominate ResNets on the performance/compute trade-off at scale, and analyzes learned attention/position-embedding structure.
